summary: Know a number tells how many are in a set or an object's position in order.
Read, write and show whole numbers from 0 to at least 31 with objects and pictures.
Count forward and backward to at least 20, with or without objects.
Find the number that is one more or one less than a given number.
Compare and put in order whole numbers from 0 to 20.
Use objects and drawings to add and subtract with numbers up to 10.
Break apart and put together numbers up to 10 using objects and pictures.
Spot, make, finish and extend simple repeating or growing patterns of shapes, colors, sounds or numbers.
Recognize basic flat and solid shapes such as squares, circles, triangles, cubes and spheres.
Sort objects by traits like shape, size, color and thickness.
Use basic shapes to model real things in the world around them.
Use words to compare objects by length, size, weight and position.
Put two or three objects in order by length or weight.
Describe numbers from 10 to 100 as tens and ones.
Read, write and represent whole numbers up to 120.
Count forward and backward from any number up to 120.
Find the number that is 10 more or 10 less than a given number.
Compare and order whole numbers up to 120.
Use words like more than, less than or about to tell how big numbers are.
Count and compare to make and read bar graphs and tally charts.
Model and solve add-to, take-from, part-whole and compare problems with objects, pictures and number lines.
Break apart and build numbers up to 12, focusing on making ten.
Link counting to adding and subtracting; skip count by 2s, 5s and 10s.
Make simple patterns and find rules to continue them; calculators may help explore.
Show real situations with basic addition and subtraction facts using objects and number sentences.
Decide whether addition and subtraction equations are true.
Find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation.
Write a number sentence with a basic fact to match a story problem.
Describe features of flat and solid shapes such as triangles, rectangles, cylinders and cones.
Combine and take apart flat and solid shapes to make new ones.
Measure an object's length by laying copies of a smaller object end to end.
Tell time to the hour and half hour.
Name pennies, nickels and dimes and total a group of them up to one dollar.
Read, write and represent whole numbers up to 1000.
Describe numbers up to 1000 as hundreds, tens and ones.
Find 10 or 100 more or less than a three-digit number.
Round numbers up or down to the nearest 10 and 100.
Compare and order whole numbers up to 1000.
Use strategies like doubles, making ten and fact families to find addition and subtraction facts.
Know basic addition facts and related subtraction facts fluently.
Estimate sums and differences up to 100.
Add and subtract two-digit numbers with place-value strategies such as partial sums.
Solve word problems adding and subtracting numbers with up to two digits.
Use adding and subtracting to make and read tables, bar graphs and tally charts.
Find and describe number patterns from repeated adding, skip counting and arrays.
Interpret addition and subtraction number sentences where a letter stands for the unknown.
Write number sentences with unknowns for situations and find values that make them true.
Sort and compare shapes by counting faces, sides, edges and corners.
Name basic flat and solid shapes such as hexagons, trapezoids, prisms and cones.
See that smaller units mean more units are needed to measure the same length.
Use a ruler to measure length to the nearest inch or centimeter.
Tell time to the quarter hour and tell a.m. from p.m.
Name coins including quarters, total their value and find coin combinations for an amount.
Read, write and represent whole numbers up to 100,000.
Describe numbers up to 100,000 by place value from ten thousands to ones.
Find 100, 1000 or 10,000 more or less than four- and five-digit numbers.
Round to the nearest 10, 100, 1000 or 10,000 and use rounding to estimate.
Compare and order whole numbers up to 100,000.
Add and subtract multi-digit numbers with place-value methods including the standard algorithm.
Solve addition and subtraction problems and check whether answers make sense.
Show multiplication and division facts with groups, arrays and number lines; relate the two operations.
Solve multiplication and division word problems, including both kinds of division situations.
Multiply a two- or three-digit number by a one-digit number using place-value strategies.
Read and write fractions as parts of a whole, parts of a set or number-line points.
Understand a fraction's size depends on the size of its whole.
Compare and order unit fractions and fractions with the same denominator using models.
Make and use one-step input-output rules with adding, subtracting or multiplying.
Interpret multiplication and division number sentences with unknowns and make up matching stories.
Write multiplication or division number sentences for problems and find the unknown values.
Identify parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to describe and draw shapes.
Sketch polygons with a given number of sides or corners.
Measure distances using half units.
Find a polygon's perimeter by adding its side lengths.
Measure the distance around real objects.
Tell time to the minute on digital and analog clocks and find elapsed time.
Know how units of time relate, such as minutes in an hour.
Make change up to one dollar in different ways, including the fewest coins.
Read an analog thermometer to the nearest degree in Fahrenheit and Celsius.
Collect data and show it in tables, bar graphs, picture graphs and line plots with scales.
Know multiplication and division facts fluently.
Use place value to multiply numbers by 10, 100 and 1000.
Multiply multi-digit numbers with place-value methods including the standard algorithm.
Estimate products and quotients by rounding to check if answers are reasonable.
Solve multi-step problems adding, subtracting and multiplying multi-digit whole numbers.
Divide multi-digit whole numbers by one- or two-digit numbers using strategies like partial quotients.
Use fraction models to show and find equivalent fractions.
Place fractions on a number line and compare fractions, mixed numbers and whole numbers.
Add and subtract fractions with like denominators using models; build a rule.
Read and write decimals and describe their place values through thousandths.
Compare and order decimals and whole numbers using place value and models.
Write tenths and hundredths as fractions and decimals; know decimal forms of halves and fourths.
Round decimals to the nearest tenth.
Make input-output rules using all four operations and record them in tables.
Interpret multiplication and division number sentences with unknowns using real situations.
Write multiplication or division number sentences for problems and solve for unknowns.
Describe, classify and sketch triangles, including equilateral, right, acute and obtuse.
Describe, classify and draw quadrilaterals such as rhombuses, trapezoids, parallelograms and kites.
Measure angles with a protractor or angle ruler.
Compare angle sizes and classify angles as acute, right or obtuse.
Find area by counting unit squares and explain why length times width works.
Find areas of figures that split into rectangles, labeling in square units.
Slide figures (translations). CCSS places transformations in grade 8.
Flip figures over vertical or horizontal lines and connect flips to lines of symmetry.
Turn figures 90 degrees clockwise or counterclockwise (rotations); CCSS grade 8 content.
Show figures are congruent using slides, flips and turns; CCSS grade 8 content.
Display data, including fractions or decimals, in tables, bar graphs, timelines and Venn diagrams.
Divide multi-digit numbers, writing quotients as remainders, fractions, mixed numbers or decimals.
Use a problem's context to choose and interpret the best form of a quotient.
Estimate answers to arithmetic problems to judge whether results are reasonable.
Solve problems using all four operations with multi-digit whole numbers.
Read and write decimals using place values from millionths to millions.
Find 0.1, 0.01 or 0.001 more or less than a number.
Order fractions and decimals, including mixed numbers, and place them on a number line.
Recognize and write equivalent decimals, fractions, mixed numbers and improper fractions.
Round numbers to the nearest tenth, hundredth or thousandth.
Add and subtract decimals and fractions using efficient methods including standard algorithms.
Model adding and subtracting fractions and decimals with different representations.
Estimate sums and differences of fractions and decimals to check reasonableness.
Solve problems adding and subtracting decimals, fractions and mixed numbers.
Use rules, tables, spreadsheets and graphs to describe patterns of change and solve problems.
Make ordered pairs from a rule or table and graph them on a coordinate grid.
Use commutative, associative, distributive properties and order of operations to write equivalent expressions.
Check whether an equation or inequality with a variable is true for a given value; CCSS grade 6.
Write equations and inequalities with variables for real situations and vice versa; CCSS grade 6.
Evaluate expressions and solve equations when variable values are given; CCSS grade 6.
Classify cubes, prisms and pyramids by counts of edges, faces and vertices and face types.
Recognize and draw nets of three-dimensional figures; CCSS grade 6.
Develop and use area formulas for triangles and parallelograms; CCSS grade 6.
Measure volume and surface area of box-shaped objects with tools and strategies.
Find volume by counting unit cubes that fill a shape; label in cubic units.
Develop and use V = lwh and V = Bh for rectangular prisms.
Find mean, median and range of data, including with a spreadsheet; CCSS grade 6.
Make and analyze double-bar and line graphs, including spreadsheet graphs.

# MDE Academic Standards: Mathematics K-12 (2007) - spreadsheet (K-5 sheet, all codes and benchmark text): https://education.mn.gov/mdeprod/idcplg?IdcService=GET_FILE&dDocName=MDE071492&RevisionSelectionMethod=latestReleased&Rendition=primary (read via Wayback snapshot 20260306045706).

# MDE Minnesota K-12 Academic Standards in Mathematics, 2007 Version - official PDF: https://education.mn.gov/mdeprod/idcplg?IdcService=GET_FILE&dDocName=005247&RevisionSelectionMethod=latestReleased&Rendition=primary (Wayback 20260306043306); codes cross-checked, 133 K-5 benchmarks in both.
# MDE Mathematics page: https://education.mn.gov/MDE/dse/stds/Math/ (Wayback 20260825094942).
# Minn. R. 3501.0750: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/3501.0750/ ; chapter table: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/3501/
# MDE timeline: https://education.mn.gov/mdeprod/idcplg?IdcService=GET_FILE&dDocName=PROD081270%20&RevisionSelectionMethod=latestReleased&Rendition=primary (Wayback 20260306061226).

# Which set is in effect: MDE Mathematics page (education.mn.gov/MDE/dse/stds/Math/, read via Wayback snapshot 2026-08-25 because the live site returns a bot-check page) says, in summary: the 2007 K-12 math standards went into effect July 2007 and are in effect through the 2026-27 school year; the 2022 standards go into effect by the beginning of 2027-28.
# Same page: MCA-III math (grades 3-8, 11) assesses the 2007 standards; MCA-IV assessing the 2022 standards is first given in 2027-28.

# Minn. R. 3501.0750 (published 2025-09-03, 49 SR 1123), subp. 6, says districts must implement these (2022) standards by the beginning of the 2027-2028 school year. The rule text holds only the anchor standards; benchmarks live in MDE's standards document.

# The 2007 rule parts (Minn. R. 3501.0700-3501.0745) now show as [Repealed, 49 SR 1123] in the rule book, yet MDE still states the 2007 standards are in effect through 2026-27; we follow MDE's statement.

# MDE Recommended Implementation Timeline (PROD081270) calls 2025-26 and 2026-27 transition years and suggests starting 2022 benchmarks early in grades K-1 (2025-26) and grade 2 (2026-27); it says districts set their own transition, the requirement being full implementation in 2027-28.
# This file: the 2007 Minnesota K-12 Academic Standards in Mathematics, the set in effect for 2026-27. The 2022 set (required from 2027-28) is in mn27.tsv.
# Code format: grade.strand.standard.benchmark, e.g. 3.1.3.2 = grade 3, strand 1 (Number & Operation), standard 3, benchmark 2. Kindergarten uses K (K.1.1.1). The coded unit is the benchmark.
# Strands (2nd code digit): 1 Number & Operation; 2 Algebra; 3 Geometry & Measurement; 4 Data Analysis (the PDF intro calls it Data Analysis and Probability; no probability benchmarks in K-5).
# Row counts: 133 benchmarks; same 47, edited 55, moved 16, new 15.

# CCSS K-5 standards not referenced by any row (absent here or only loosely present): K.OA.A.4 K.OA.A.5 K.NBT.A.1 K.G.A.3 K.G.B.4 K.G.B.6 1.OA.A.2 1.OA.B.4 1.NBT.C.4 1.NBT.C.6 1.G.A.3 2.OA.C.3 2.NBT.B.6 2.NBT.B.7 2.MD.A.3 2.MD.A.4 2.MD.B.5 2.MD.B.6 2.MD.D.9 2.G.A.2 2.G.A.3 3.OA.B.5 3.NBT.A.3 3.MD.A.2 3.G.A.2 4.OA.B.4 4.NF.B.4 4.MD.A.2 4.MD.C.7 5.NF.B.4 5.NF.B.5 5.NF.B.6 5.NF.B.7 5.MD.A.1 5.MD.B.2 5.G.B.3 5.G.B.4. Notably: teen numbers as ten plus ones (K.NBT.A.1), making ten (K.OA.A.4), partitioning shapes into halves/thirds/fourths (1.G.A.3, 2.G.A.3), length on a number line (2.MD.B.6), multiplying fractions by whole numbers (4.NF.B.4) and all of grade-5 fraction multiplication/division (5.NF.B.4-7, in Minnesota grade 6), unit conversion (5.MD.A.1), line plots with fractions (5.MD.B.2).

# Notable non-CCSS or earlier-than-CCSS content: patterns in K-1 (K.2.1.1, 1.2.1.1); money from grade 1 (1.3.2.3); rounding in grade 2 (2.1.1.4); numbers to 100,000 and multiplying by one-digit in grade 3; thermometer reading (3.3.3.4); translations, rotations, congruence in grade 4 (4.3.3.x, CCSS grade 8); thousandths decimals in grade 4; variables, equations and inequalities in grade 5 (5.2.3.x, CCSS grade 6); nets, triangle/parallelogram area, mean/median/range in grade 5 (CCSS grade 6); spreadsheets in data benchmarks.

# Uncertainties: several benchmarks span two CCSS grades (e.g. 3.1.2.1 standard algorithm, 4.1.1.3, 4.1.1.6); kind=edited was used when a same-grade code fits part of the benchmark. 3.1.1.3 and 3.3.3.3 are mapped to grade-2 analogues (2.NBT.B.8, 2.MD.C.8) as moved; 2.1.2.3 estimation mapped to 3.OA.D.8 as moved; 5.1.2.2 (0.1/0.01/0.001 more or less) marked new. Summaries are paraphrases, not official text.
# Mapping notes: no official Minnesota-to-CCSS crosswalk exists (Minnesota did not adopt CCSS math); all ccss values are this file's own judgment from reading both texts.

# kind: same = CCSS standard at the same grade with essentially the same content; edited = same-grade CCSS counterpart but range, scope or emphasis differs (extra codes from other grades may be listed); moved = only CCSS counterpart is at another K-5 grade; new = no CCSS K-5 counterpart (includes content CCSS places in grade 6-8; those codes are not listed because only K-5 codes are allowed).
# ccss codes are listed at standard level (no sub-letters such as 4.NF.B.4a).
